items.Sentence: The tasting room and hospitality building will be served by a 1,500-gallon kitchen grease interceptor, designed for a maximum flow of 500 gpd and a 3-day retention time. The precast concrete grease interceptor is intended to remove oil and grease from the kitchen wastewater.

A 1,500-gallon precast concrete septic tank with effluent filter will serve the MA residence. The septic tank is designed to provide a 3-day detention time for solids removal prior to effluent entering the larger winery septic tank. A 13,000-gallon fiberglass septic tank with effluent filter will serve the entire Facility. The 13,000-gallon septic tank is designed to provide a 3-day detention time for solids removal and to act as a sump prior to transferring effluent to the Advantex pretreatment system.
The 13,000 gallon septic tank will be equipped with duplex pumps and float switches that will be controlled and monitored by an adjacent pump control panel with visual and audible alarm.

A wastewater treatment system, consisting of an Advantex recirculating aerobic biological filter system, will be installed to provide secondary level treatment for the domestic wastewater flow. The treatment system consists of one filter unit, a recirculation tank, dosing tank, piping, pumps, and controls. The filter unit, also referred to as a treatment pod, is a manufacturer-supplied modular unit consisting of a fiberglass tank containing textile filtration media, a pressurized influent distribution pipe network, and an underdrain to collect treated wastewater.
The treatment system consists of one filter unit, a recirculation tank, dosing tank, piping, pumps, and controls.

Following secondary level treatment, effluent will be disinfected and disposed of at a subsurface drip disposal field. A flow meter will measure the volume of effluent being sent to the disposal field. A UV disinfection basin outfitted with a UV unit rated for 83 gallons per minute (gpm) will provide disinfection prior to subsurface disposal. The UV system manufacturers cited water quality recommendation of a maximum concentration of 10 mg/L suspended solids prior to UV light exposure.

Following secondary level treatment, effluent will be disinfected and disposed of at a subsurface drip disposal field. A subsurface drip disposal field will be located in a vineyard on the north end of the parcel near Sausal Creek. The disposal field is designed to dispose of 4,025 gpd of effluent with an application rate of 1.2 gallons/square foot/day.
